claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me ask you a few questions.

**First, could you tell me the names and ages of the child or children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great that you're checking on this.

Since Alex is 16, there are specific rules that apply. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, this could be school, college, university, or a government-approved training scheme.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex actually left school recently, but they've just registered with the local careers service to get some guidance on what to do next - you know, figuring out their options for college or work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know! Since Alex has registered with the local careers service after leaving education, this is actually a positive factor for your eligibility.

**Can you confirm - has Alex been registered with the careers service for less than 20 weeks since they left school?** This is important because you can typically claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks in this situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's been less than 20 weeks. They only just signed up recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's very useful information. Let me just confirm one more thing to complete the picture.

**Are you currently living with Alex, or are you contributing towards their upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex is 16 and living with you** – This means you meet the basic requirement of being responsible for a child and living with them.
- **Alex has registered with the local careers service** – Even though Alex has left school, registering with a government-sponsored careers service (like your local careers service) is one of the exceptions that allows you to continue claiming Child Benefit.
- **You're within the 20-week window** – You can claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when Alex left education, as long as they remain registered with the careers service during this period.

**Important note:** Your eligibility will continue as long as Alex remains registered with the careers service within that 20-week period. If Alex starts full-time paid work (24 hours or more per week), begins an apprenticeship, or the 20 weeks pass without them moving into approved education or training, your eligibility will end.

If you haven't already, you can make a claim for Child Benefit through the usual channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
